items.t: Vogue sent robots down the runway at Vogue World, and people were not impressed
items.d: Nothing says Italian craftsmanship like a Chinese robot doing a lasso to "L'Amour Toujours."
items.fullText: Vogue World closed its Milan edition this week with a troupe of robots — perhaps a preview of what’s coming when the event descends on San Francisco next year. Vogue World is the magazine’s annual traveling spectacle, now in its fifth year: part runway show, part celebrity showcase, part variety hour, part ad-sales opportunity , staged in a different city each time. It has run through New York, London, Paris, and Hollywood. This year’s Milan edition was marketed as a tribute to Italian craftsmanship and “the human touch” in an age of technology, which makes what happened next a little strange. During the act titled The Age of Intelligence, humanoid robots made by the Chinese firm Unitree walked into the Galleria to Gigi D’Agostino’s “L’Amour Toujours.” They waved their arms in the air, imploring onlookers to clap. One did a lasso. They were not wearing clothes. The pained expression of Alessandro Michele, the creative director of Valentino, quickly went viral. Vogue World Milano ends (appropriately Europoor-kitschily) with tiny robottini dancing to L’Amour Toujours while Alessandro Michele slowly dies inside pic.twitter.com/xicYWWl6VW — sascha (@SaschaAmato) September 22, 2026 I haven’t seen a single thing about the actual fashion that was presented at Vogue World Milan. Instead, everyone is talking about the robots. (These same robots have been making headlines worldwide for their dance moves , and for falling and breaking .) Similar robots turned up on the runway at London Fashion Week, which is happening now. Vogue turned heads earlier this year when it announced that the next edition will be in San Francisco, arguably one of the least stylish cities in the United States. The timing isn’t coincidental. items.fullText: 전국 새만금개발청, 현대차그룹 'AI 데이터센터' 건축심의 본격 착수 발행일 : 2026-09-24 08:00 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 현대차그룹의 새만금에 9조원 투자 발표. 새만금개발청(청장 문성요)은 새만금 1산단 7공구에 착공하는 현대자동차그룹의 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터(AI DC) 건축계획(안)에 대한 건축심의에 착수했다고 24일 밝혔다. 현대자동차그룹은 지난 2월 27일 자율자동차와 로봇 학습을 지원하기 위해 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 5만장을 투입해 새만금에 5조8000억원 규모의 AI DC를 구축하는 등 약 9조원을 투자하기로 발표한 바 있다. 2027년 3월 AI DC 착공을 시작으로 그해 말 태양광 발전 및 수소 생산시설도 단계적으로 착공할 예정이다. 새만금개발청은 2027년 3월 AI DC 착공 등 현대자동차그룹의 투자 실행을 뒷받침하기 위해 이번 건축심의를 신속하게 진행할 계획이다. 현대자동차그룹 AI DC는 대지면적 15만312㎡, 연면적 10만1950㎡, 지상 2층 규모의 방송통신시설로 자율차·로봇 등 피지컬 AI 기술을 뒷받침할 핵심 인프라가 될 전망이다. 새만금개발청은 현대자동차그룹 AI DC 건축계획을 내실 있게 검토하기 위해 분야별 민간 전문가 25명과 당연직 위원 5명 등 총 30명으로 건축위원회를 구성했다. 데이터센터라는 건축물의 특성을 감안하여 건축계획, 구조안전, 도시계획, 경관, 시공, 방재, 교통 등 다양한 분야의 전문가를 위원으로 위촉했다.. 특히 연면적 4만3000㎡를 초과하는 대규모 시설인 만큼, 교통 혼잡 예방 및 효율적인 진출입 체계 구축을 위해 교통 분야 전문가를 전체 위원의 4분의 1 수준(7명)으로 대폭 강화했다. 이번 심의는 서면 심의로 진행할 예정이며, 위원들의 면밀한 검토를 거쳐 10월 중 심의 결과가 나올 예정이다. 심의 결과를 토대로, 건축허가와 산단 입주절차(입주계약 등)를 병행 진행해 연내 건축허가를 완료하는 신속 · 적극 행정을 실천할 계획이다. 문성요 새만금개발청장은 “이번 AI DC 건축심의는 현대자동차그룹의 새만금 투자 이행이 가시화되는 첫 출발점”이라며, “전문가들의 심의를 거쳐 안전하고 효율적인 건축물이 만들어질 수 있도록 행정적 지원을 아끼지 않겠다”고 말했다. 군산=김한식 기자 hskim@etnews.com

items.t: VC firm Bessemer now has another $5.75B to invest in (what else?) AI
items.d: The VC firm says that AI-native companies are growing faster than any technology, ever.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 1:35 PM PDT · September 23, 2026 Image Credits: TechCrunch (AI-generated) Julie Bort VC firm Bessemer now has another $5.75B to invest in (what else?) AI Bessemer Venture Partners announced on Wednesday that it has raised $5.75 billion across two new funds to accelerate its investment across all parts of the AI stack. The firm, which has backed companies such as Anthropic, Cognition, Legora, Perplexity, Ramp, Shopify, and Waymo, dedicated $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and the remaining $4 billion for growth startups. Bessemer has been well-known as a leading VC in the SaaS era , with a particular knack for picking enterprise winners, like Box, Docusign, and Gainsight. Since 2022, it has invested in more than 260 AI-native companies. So far, the firm has invested $3 billion into AI-related startups, it says, including those focused on compute, infrastructure, foundation models, dev tools, app-layer startups, and agentic tech. Now, Bessemer positions all things AI as the opportunity of a lifetime — a common sentiment, until the next big trendy tech revolution comes around, of course. “AI-native companies are scaling faster than any category of technology we’ve backed before,” Bessemer Partner Byron Deeter said in the company’s funding announcement. VC firms also need to keep increasing their war chests, Deeter told Bloomberg , because companies staying private longer has become “a permanent structural shift.” Topics Bessemer Venture Partners , In Brief , TC , Venture October 13 – 15 San Francisco Your next big connection is at Disrupt. items.t: Disney+ and Hulu add to the growing trend of streaming inflation
items.d: At the same time, Disney appears to be exploring new ways to expand its streaming business beyond simply raising subscription prices.
items.fullText: Streaming is getting more expensive again. Disney is the latest media giant to raise prices for its streaming services, adding to a growing pattern across the industry. The increases come roughly a year after Disney’s last major streaming price hike . Disney is raising the price of its ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle to $21.99 a month, up from $19.99, whereas the ad-free stand-alone plans are each rising to $21.49 per month, up from $18.99. The company is also increasing the price of its stand-alone ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans to $12.49 a month. The new prices are reflected on Disney+’s support page . Bloomberg was the first to report the changes. Disney+ and Hulu are hardly alone. Streaming companies have spent the past several years steadily increasing prices. Peacock and Apple TV also raised prices in August, while Netflix increased prices earlier this year. When Disney+ launched in 2019, its basic monthly subscription cost $6.99. Since then, the service has gradually moved further away from that intro price as Disney has tried to turn streaming into a profitable part of its entertainment business. The latest increases come as streaming remains an increasingly important part of Disney’s overall business. In its third-quarter 2026 results , Disney said entertainment streaming revenue from Disney+ and Hulu rose 11% to $5.5 billion, driven by subscriber growth and the impact of previous price increases. At the same time, Disney appears to be exploring new ways to expand its streaming business beyond simply raising subscription prices. The company has reportedly explored the possibility of introducing a free tier for Disney+. This could put the company in more direct competition with platforms such as YouTube and Tubi, which have been capturing a growing share of consumers’ viewing time. items.fullText: 판타지의 경계를 확장하다: 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지가 도쿄게임쇼 2026에서 펼치는 캐릭터 IP와 리테일의 미래 2026/09/23 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 9월 17일부터 20일까지 일본 지바현 마쿠하리 멧세(Makuhari Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 있다. 관람객 다니엘 아세로(Daniel Acero) 씨는 “처음 봤을 때 스크린 화면인 줄 전혀 몰랐고, 투명한 설치물이라고 생각했다”면서 “마치 화면 뒤에 실제 공간이 있는 것처럼 깊이감이 느껴져서 놀라웠고, 이러한 방식으로 게임 캐릭터를 소개하면 게임에 대한 관심을 높이고 캐릭터의 개성을 효과적으로 전달할 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 관람객 동선과 items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning, using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. items.fullText: University of Manchester Uses NVIDIA Earth-2 to Forecast Air Pollution Across the UK Manchester physicists David Topping and Hao Zhang applied NVIDIA Earth-2 generative models to air quality forecasting — unlocking predictions fast enough to inform public health. September 15, 2026 by Isha Salian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. September 15, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Know everything. Do anything. That was the message NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang brought to Salesforce Dreamforce Tuesday, joining CEO Marc Benioff onstage in an appearance that coincided with the announcement of Koa — Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang didn’t just take the stage. He walked into the crowd — threading through the audience at Moscone Center, mic in hand, with Benioff alongside. “We’re all following you, bro,” Benioff told Huang at one point, drawing applause. “With electricity, we could power everything,” Huang said, tracing the arc of industrial revolutions. “With the internet, you can find anything. And now, with artificial intelligence as an infrastructure layer across the planet, we can know everything and do anything.” That arc led directly to the announcement. Salesforce’s first reasoning model was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on a proprietary synthetic dataset drawn from nearly three decades of enterprise CRM deployments. items.fullText: Skild AI Taps NVIDIA Physical AI to Teach Robots New Tasks From a Single Video Skild AI’s S1 robotic foundation model harnesses NVIDIA technologies spanning synthetic data generation, model training, simulation and real-world deployment. September 10, 2026 by Sasa Docca 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Manufacturing floors, warehouses and production lines rarely stay fixed — tasks change, layouts shift and new products arrive, and most robots can’t keep up without significant reprogramming. Skild AI’s new S1 robot foundation model helps address this, designed to learn previously unseen, long-horizon tasks from a single video demonstration. The model, launched last week, uses video as input to understand and execute the task without updating its weights or undergoing task-specific post-training — a technique called in-context learning. Skild built S1 and conducted the research on NVIDIA AI infrastructure, part of a broader collaboration spanning synthetic data generation, model training, simulation and real-world physical AI deployment. The companies are working together to move adaptable robot intelligence from the lab into factories and other dynamic operating environments. “Learning by experience, and not preprogramming, is the step change that has happened in robotics,” said Deepak Pathak, cofounder and CEO of Skild AI. “NVIDIA Isaac Lab and NVIDIA Cosmos technologies help Skild create the scalable, diverse experience its robots need to learn across many scenarios and embodiments.” The launch comes as the company reached a $100 million annual revenue run rate 10 months after its first commercial deployment. In that time, Skild has built more than 60 deployment partnerships with work spanning manufacturing, logistics, inspection, security, food preparation and other applications.
